newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may send Perry to talks with Gulf allies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may send Perry to talks with Gulf allies.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Perry may travel to the Gulf region this weekend to discuss the Iraq situation with U.S. friends and allies there, adminstration officials said on Friday.
"A trip is under consideration for Secretary Perry (but) a final decision has not been made," one official told Reuters.
U.S. officials said the countries on the proposed intinerary would be Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain and "maybe Turkey."

The trip was discussed Friday morning at a meeting of President Bill Clinton's top national security advisers and was expected to be discussed at another meeting later on Friday between Clinton and those same advisers, one official said.
The thinking is that Perry -- not Secretary of State Warren Christopher or some other senior official -- would go because "the focus right now is the military aspect," he said.

"The purpose of the Perry trip would be to talk to regional players ... (about) providing the support we would need to carry out various operations in the region and to explain exactly what possible missions might be, in this case to keep the no-fly zone effectively in force," the official added.

Although Iraq and the United States signaled willingness on Friday to end their face-off, the Pentagon said it would watch and continue for now to build a Gulf strike force of attack jets and warships.
The United States has been building up its forces in the Gulf region for possible military strikes designed to punish Iraq for challenging allied air patrols in no-fly zones.
